film: TAKEDA 2040 — What We Must Build Today to Shape the Future of Medicine

scenes.title: The defining question
scenes.purpose: Pose the film's question from Takeda's own position, not from competitors.
scenes.takeaway: One medicine carries 21% of revenue and is dated; the question is what makes success repeatable.
scenes.narration: A single medicine can carry a company. At Takeda, Entyvio is twenty-one percent of revenue, and its exclusivity ends in the second half of this decade. But every medicine sits inside a wider system: science, data, manufacturing, evidence, partners, patients. So the question for the next fifteen years is not which drug comes next. It is what makes success repeatable.
scenes.accuracy_notes: 21% is Takeda's FY2025 disclosure (April 2025–March 2026). 'Second half of this decade' is Takeda's own wording for loss of regulatory exclusivity; exact biosimilar timing is uncertain per the same filing.

visual.composition: A single red pill-shaped mark centre frame on near-black; the camera pulls back and the mark becomes the hub of a six-node capability ring (science, data, manufacturing, evidence, partners, patients). Title card 'TAKEDA 2040' resolves at the end.

scenes.title: Lesson one: concentration cuts both ways (Lilly)
scenes.purpose: Use Lilly as evidence that one-franchise growth creates exposure before LOE.
scenes.takeaway: Growth concentrated in one molecule brings price and payer exposure early.
scenes.narration: Eli Lilly grew from twenty-eight to sixty-five billion dollars in four years; tirzepatide became fifty-six percent of its sales. But concentration cuts both ways: by late twenty twenty-six, realized prices had fallen fifteen percent, and one pharmacy benefit manager kept Lilly's drug off its preferred list for fifteen months. A single franchise creates exposure long before any patent expires.
scenes.accuracy_notes: USD 28,318m FY2021 → USD 65,179m FY2025 (US GAAP, 10-K). Tirzepatide = Mounjaro + Zepbound, 56.0% of FY2025 revenue (computed from 10-K tables). Price decline is Lilly's Q3 2026 statement (realised prices -15% YoY). CVS Caremark removed Zepbound from commercial template formularies 1 Jul 2025 and restored it 1 Oct 2026 (15 months, computed). 'Long before any patent expires': tirzepatide patent 2036 (CLM-000250).

scenes.title: Lesson two: the successor must exist before the cliff (AbbVie)
scenes.purpose: Show the one competitor mechanism that transfers cleanly to Takeda's Entyvio problem.
scenes.takeaway: Replacement worked because successors were already marketed; contracting only delays.
scenes.narration: AbbVie faced the cliff Takeda now faces. Humira fell from twenty-one billion dollars to four and a half billion within three years of biosimilar entry. Yet AbbVie recovered, because Skyrizi and Rinvoq were already on the market, across Humira's major indications. Contracting held ninety-seven percent of volume for over a year. It delayed the fall. It did not prevent it.
scenes.accuracy_notes: Humira global net revenue USD 21,237m (2022) → 4,540m (2025); U.S. biosimilar entry began January 2023. AbbVie total revenue dipped in 2023 and exceeded the 2022 peak only in 2025 (CLM-003015). Skyrizi + Rinvoq USD 7,687m → 25,866m. '≥97% of U.S. adalimumab volume through March 2024' (14 months after entry) is a trade-press/IQVIA figure, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED. Steep U.S. declines followed the April 2024 CVS formulary change (association, not proven causation, CLM-003010).

scenes.title: Lesson three: diversification works; AI has no outcome yet (J&J and all four)
scenes.purpose: Close the competitor act with the diversification lesson and the honest AI reality check.
scenes.takeaway: Diversified bases absorb cliffs; no AI programme in the study has an independent outcome.
scenes.narration: Johnson and Johnson absorbed a forty-one percent fall in Stelara with a diversified base; its largest brand is only fifteen percent of sales. And artificial intelligence? Across all four companies, the research found no independent evidence that any AI programme has yet changed a cost, a timeline, or a revenue line. Lilly built an open robotic laboratory, then sold it. Announcements are not outcomes.

Lilly's Life Sciences Studio was acquired by Arctoris (a CRO) in 2024; Lilly's reason is undisclosed (CLM-006017, contested).

scenes.title: The central challenge
scenes.purpose: Quantify Takeda's dated exposure and state the task.
scenes.takeaway: Defend what is dated; build what repeats.
scenes.narration: Takeda. Entyvio brings in nine hundred fifty-eight billion yen. Medicare price negotiation takes effect in January twenty twenty-eight, and two biosimilar applications are already under FDA review. Vyvanse lost two hundred twenty billion yen in two years. If Entyvio erodes the way Humira did, three hundred eighty to seven hundred seventy billion yen a year is at risk; a scenario, not a forecast. But it defines the task: defend what is dated, and build what repeats.

kinds.range 383–766bn: SCENARIO (ASM-024: 40–80% erosion over three years applied to JPY 958.0bn; not a forecast)

scenes.accuracy_notes: Entyvio JPY 958.0bn FY2025. CMS selected Entyvio in January 2026 for a negotiated price effective January 2028. Two vedolizumab biosimilar BLAs accepted for FDA review (Alvotech AVT16; Fresenius Kabi/Polpharma PB016). Vyvanse JPY 423.2bn (FY2023) → 203.2bn (FY2025) = −220.0bn. Scenario range = 40%/80% × 958.0 = 383/766 JPY bn per year; the base is global while first entry is a U.S. event, so the range overstates the first three years (stated in the strategy).

scenes.title: What Takeda already has
scenes.purpose: Establish the baseline strengths so recommendations build on them, not around them.
scenes.takeaway: Plasma scale, in-house orexin science, late-stage execution and stop discipline are evidenced strengths.
scenes.narration: Takeda is not starting from zero. More than two hundred seventy plasma centres, with fractionation capacity expanding. Its Shonan labs discovered oveporexton, approved in August twenty twenty-six for narcolepsy. Rusfertide followed; zasocitinib is under priority review. Three Phase three readouts came in positive, on plan. And Takeda has shown it can stop: it exited cell therapy and took the write-down.
scenes.accuracy_notes: 'More than 270' is Takeda's FY2025 wording (275 in FY2024). USD 230m Los Angeles expansion announced June 2024 (up to 2m litres/yr). Oveporexton (Orzeyful) FDA approval 5 Aug 2026 for narcolepsy type 1; discovered in Shonan per Takeda. Rusfertide (Mimrylo) approved 28 Aug 2026 (licensed from Protagonist). Zasocitinib NDA accepted under Priority Review 14 Sep 2026 (Nimbus acquisition). Dec-2024 R&D Day planned three 2025 readouts; all three read out positive (company-reported). Cell-therapy exit: JPY 58.2bn impairment (FY2025 20-F); soticlestat discontinued Jan 2025.

scenes.title: From products to repeatable scientific advantage
scenes.purpose: Introduce the first build: proprietary decision-linked data as the compounding asset.
scenes.takeaway: Compute and models are purchasable; decision-linked data is not. Build the governed data and decision layer.
scenes.narration: What should Takeda build first? What rivals cannot buy. Compute can be rented and models are converging; what stays proprietary is the data a company generates when it decides. AbbVie connected two thousand trials into one research hub with fewer than ten staff. It has published no outcome yet. Takeda's version: a governed data and decision layer, where every experiment and every go or no-go is logged against a baseline.
scenes.accuracy_notes: ARCH: conceived 2020, built by fewer than ten full-time AbbVie staff plus contractors; 2,000+ trials' de-identified data reusable internally (company statements at Bio-IT World 2023). 'Over USD 1bn' is Lilly's own estimate of historical data cost. 'Models are converging' is the strategy's INTERPRETATION of shared federated models (TuneLab, AISB).

The red layer then becomes a ledger: experiment → decision → baseline → measured effect, rows writing themselves.

scenes.title: Data as a strategic asset: baseline first, then claim
scenes.purpose: Convert the data theme into a measurement discipline Takeda can apply immediately.
scenes.takeaway: Takeda has adoption; it needs measured value with independent ownership.
scenes.narration: Takeda already has the platform. Sixty-three percent of the workforce uses generative AI. But usage is adoption, not value. At Lessines, one hundred seventy predictive-maintenance agents run; their savings are unpublished. Baseline first, then claim. And whoever measures should not own the savings target.

scenes.title: The intelligent laboratory
scenes.purpose: Separate established automation from emerging and undemonstrated autonomy; recommend rent-and-gate.
scenes.takeaway: Climb the automation ladder only when triggers fire; gate AI partners on first-in-human data.
scenes.narration: In the laboratory, the same rule applies. Scripted automation, robots that dose, measure and screen, is mature and sold as a service. Remote cloud labs work but have proved commercially fragile. An AI that plans its own experiments is a prototype; first clinical data from such partnerships is still a year or two away. A fully autonomous discovery loop has not been demonstrated anywhere. So: rent automation, climb only when triggers fire, and gate the AI partners on first-in-human data.

kinds.CLM-006051: FACT (industry case, not one of the four)

scenes.accuracy_notes: Ladder: scripted automation operational/commodity (Arctoris platform, Lilly Lebanon robots); remote cloud lab operational but commercially fragile (Lilly's Studio divested to a CRO; Zymergen distressed sale as industry calibration); AI-planned loop prototype–pilot (Nabla expects first-in-human data within one to two years of Oct 2025; NVIDIA–Lilly lab is an announcement); autonomous end-to-end discovery with clinical outcome: not demonstrated in any source opened. Takeda partners: Nabla (> USD 1bn success-based), Iambic (> USD 1.7bn success-based).

scenes.title: Commercial execution and care: the whole value chain
scenes.purpose: Connect evidence to access decisions and patients; set honest expectations for Entyvio defence.
scenes.takeaway: Delay and measure erosion; resolve the channel question; be the first to measure patient outcomes.
scenes.narration: Pharmacy benefit managers now decide biosimilar outcomes: when CVS moved its templates to Stelara biosimilars, most members paid nothing. The Entyvio plan is honest: delay erosion, and measure it. The subcutaneous pen drives uptake and the HYHUB device brings plasma therapy home. But the pharmacy channel is also where biosimilars win. No company studied publishes adherence outcomes; Takeda can be the first, starting with the oveporexton launch.

kinds.CLM-007039: FACT (INCONCLUSIVE: absence of published outcomes in sources opened)

scenes.accuracy_notes: CVS Health: from 1 Jul 2026 its most common commercial template formularies prefer interchangeable Stelara biosimilars, most members paying $0. Benefit-channel gate (medical vs pharmacy split) is RM-003, 2027 H1, an ASSUMPTION; the registry has no Entyvio channel split. Entyvio SC 'continues to drive increased patient uptake' per Takeda's 20-F; HYHUB/HYHUB DUO 510(k) July 2025 for home transfer of Hyqvia. The SC-vs-PBM tension is the strategy's stated BET-04/BET-11 conflict. No source opened for any of the four companies reports adherence or persistence outcomes for patient programmes.

scenes.title: Partnerships, acquisitions and the leverage test
scenes.purpose: Show Takeda's actual external-innovation instrument and why the large acquisition is rejected.
scenes.takeaway: Mid-size licensing fits the leverage ceiling; options are unproven; a USD 5bn purchase fails the arithmetic.
scenes.narration: Takeda's instrument for partnerships is the mid-sized licence: Nimbus for four billion dollars upfront, Innovent for one point two. AbbVie runs early options worth up to a billion a year, yet none signed in this period has produced an approved product. AbbVie wrote off half of Cerevel within months. At two point six times leverage, with Amitiza pending, a five billion dollar purchase fails the arithmetic. Fund a licensing channel instead, released when leverage allows.

kinds.CLM-005005: FACT (2.6x at Mar 2026 confirmed by audit)

scenes.accuracy_notes: Nimbus: USD 4.0bn upfront (Feb 2023) + up to USD 2bn milestones. Innovent: USD 1.2bn upfront incl. USD 100m equity (Oct 2025). AbbVie 'other' upfront stream USD 0.6–1.0bn/yr. 'No option from the window has produced an approved product' is the comparison's finding (HYPOTHESIS about durability). Emraclidine: Phase 2 miss Nov 2024, USD 4.5bn impairment in Q4 2024 (Cerevel closed Aug 2024). Leverage 2.6x adjusted net debt/EBITDA at 31 Mar 2026; Amitiza provision JPY 403.5bn. '5bn fails the arithmetic' is the council's computation (≈3.1x, ≈3.4x if the provision is debt-funded) against a 3.0x planning ceiling, ignoring free cash flow. Cerevel consideration USD 8.7bn (USD 8.3bn net of cash), closed 2024-08-01 [CLM-009053]; USD 4.5bn emraclidine impairment recorded after the November 2024 EMPOWER failures [CLM-009054].

visual.composition: A deal-flow diagram: a middle lane of licences (Nimbus 4.0, Innovent 1.2) in red; a lower lane of small option chips in grey with a 'approved products from options: 0' counter; an upper lane with a large acquisition block (Cerevel) that cracks and loses 4.5. A leverage gauge needle at 2.6x swings past a red 3.0x ceiling when a '+USD 5bn' weight is dropped on. The licence lane gets a 'released when leverage allows' gate.

scenes.title: Long-term compounding: what the platform analogies really say
scenes.purpose: Use the Module 2 analogies to set realistic expectations for platform bets.
scenes.takeaway: Platforms compound slowly and protect no single product; cap the long bets and compound Takeda's own strengths.
scenes.narration: And the platform dream? NVIDIA says CUDA made no money for ten years. SpaceX built Falcon nine for a fraction of NASA's estimate. Alphabet's other bets lost seven and a half billion dollars in twenty twenty-five alone. Regeneron's discovery platform did not stop its lead product falling forty-two percent. Platforms compound slowly and protect no single product. So Takeda's long bets are capped options with stop rules, and the strengths it compounds are its own: plasma process data, and orexin biology.
scenes.accuracy_notes: CUDA: NVIDIA's Ian Buck (March 2026) said CUDA cost billions and NVIDIA 'didn't make money for 10 years' on it. Falcon 9 + Falcon 1 development ≈ USD 390m (SpaceX figure verified by NASA) vs NASA model estimates USD 1.7–4.0bn. Alphabet Other Bets operating loss USD 7,515m in 2025 (incl. a USD 2.1bn Waymo compensation charge). EYLEA U.S. net sales −42% in 2025 (competition and the shift to EYLEA HD). The film labels these as analogies; the strategy treats them as hypothesis generators.

scenes.title: Execution: the sequence, the gates, the envelope
scenes.purpose: Give leadership the first three years, the gate logic and the honest size of the ask.
scenes.takeaway: Start everything measurable in 2027; decide at dated gates; the envelope is a gated planning assumption.
scenes.narration: The sequence. Twenty twenty-seven: baselines, the data standard, rented automation and the Entyvio channel decision, together. Twenty twenty-eight: the Medicare price lands, the biosimilar playbook goes live, the AI partnerships face a go or no-go on data. The balanced envelope is about one point nine billion dollars over fourteen years, roughly three percent of today's R and D, plus a contingent pool for licences: planning assumptions, not a budget. The council that challenged this plan found no funded bet robust to severe pricing pressure; hence the gates.
scenes.accuracy_notes: Dates are roadmap v2 milestones (ASSUMPTION) except the Medicare effective date (FACT). Envelope: balanced USD 1,920m committed at gates, cumulative 2027–2040, plus ~USD 1,030m contingent headroom for BET-18; roughly 3.0% of fourteen years of flat R&D (JPY 675.9bn FY2025 at ASM-001 150 JPY/USD). Takeda's actual budget is not public (IVB-014). The council's stress test rated no funded bet robust under SCN-3 (pricing/biosimilar pressure).

scenes.title: Closing: build the system around the medicines
scenes.takeaway: No single drug, deal or technology secures the decade; a repeatable, measured, connected organisation does.
scenes.narration: No single drug secures the next decade. No acquisition. No technology. What endures is an organisation that discovers repeatedly, measures honestly, connects evidence to patients, and learns faster than the market moves. Takeda has the raw material: a franchise to defend, launches in hand, plasma and orexin to compound, and the discipline to stop. Build the system around them. Start in twenty twenty-seven. Measure from day one. Decide at every gate.
scenes.accuracy_notes: The closing restates the strategy's RECOMMENDATIONS; every 'raw material' item is a FACT established in S06. No claim of eliminating LOE is made.
